facts.label: Recovery operand consequences
facts.text: DIP non-objection/subordination requires DIP principal plus specified senior borrowed-money principal and LC face within Maximum First Lien Indebtedness Amount plus USD10m; exclusions from that test do not remove broader discharge obligations. The maximum refers to indenture §4.09(b)(1), with reduction/increase qualifications—not automatically USD90m. Junior AP additional/replacement liens and administrative claims require specified senior priority; cash AP remains objectionable. Pay-over is limited to the lesser of junior receipts and senior cash shortfall, with the prescribed equal-value property exchange (ICA pp.7–8 L349–L373).

facts.label: Recovery operand consequences
facts.text: Discharge requires the specified cash payments, hedge/bank-product satisfaction or collateralization and transaction termination, commitment termination, and LC termination or satisfactory cash collateralization no greater than 105% of aggregate undrawn LC face; undemanded indemnities receive the stated exception (ICA p.1 L62). Refinancing can deem discharge not to have occurred; avoidance restores obligations and the ICA. After genuine discharge, remaining senior obligations receive only the stated pari passu benefits, subject to §5.6 (pp.6–8 L325–L337, L375–L378). Releases require the §5.1 enforcement or permitted-disposition conditions; guarantee release is linked to all-equity sale and senior guarantee release. Ordinary dispositions require senior permission and no express junior prohibition. A cash bid buys Collateral, not senior debt; junior credit bidding requires cash sufficient to cause senior discharge. No standalone debt-buyout option is identified in the examined ICA; other documents remain missing (§3.1(e), §6.12).

facts.label: Recovery intake conclusion
facts.text: The positive finding is contractual access asymmetry, not a quantified loss. Conditionally, declaration/demand and receipt initiate restrictions; loss of unilateral realization timing is the first legal break. If assets deteriorate during delay, senior accruals or qualifying financing could absorb more proceeds; a conditioned sale/release could replace guarantee/asset access with residual proceeds. Observable tests are notices, diligence/stay filings, claims, valuations, DIP/AP orders, sale consideration and discharge records—not assumed issuer events.

facts.label: Recovery intake conclusion
facts.text: The strongest countercase combines reciprocal grants and matching-collateral intent, residual proceeds, qualified payments, conditional bidding/AP rights and anti-disproportionate-amendment safeguards (§§2.3–2.4,5.3). It wins economically if verified coextensive perfected coverage, immaterial exceptions and ample net value after actual senior claims are demonstrated. Control asymmetry alone cannot defeat that case or establish the fulcrum.

| Dynamic priorities | CP-4D T4F.4–5 adopts conditional DIP/AP, refinancing continuity, avoidance reinstatement, bid/release and postdischarge rules (ICA pp.5–8 §§5.1,5.5–5.6,6.1–6.13). | Obtain financing/orders, cap formula/usage, AP payments, sale/release terms, avoidance and discharge records. Preserve conditions explained below. | Priority and reachable support must be tested by event, not frozen as two static balances. No financing headroom or recovery follows. |

DIP non-objection/subordination requires DIP principal plus specified senior borrowed-money principal and LC face within Maximum First Lien Indebtedness Amount plus USD10m; exclusions from that test do not remove broader discharge obligations. The maximum refers to indenture §4.09(b)(1), with reduction/increase qualifications—not automatically USD90m. Junior AP additional/replacement liens and administrative claims require specified senior priority; cash AP remains objectionable. Pay-over is limited to the lesser of junior receipts and senior cash shortfall, with the prescribed equal-value property exchange (ICA pp.7–8 L349–L373).

Discharge requires the specified cash payments, hedge/bank-product satisfaction or collateralization and transaction termination, commitment termination, and LC termination or satisfactory cash collateralization no greater than 105% of aggregate undrawn LC face; undemanded indemnities receive the stated exception (ICA p.1 L62). Refinancing can deem discharge not to have occurred; avoidance restores obligations and the ICA. After genuine discharge, remaining senior obligations receive only the stated pari passu benefits, subject to §5.6 (pp.6–8 L325–L337, L375–L378). Releases require the §5.1 enforcement or permitted-disposition conditions; guarantee release is linked to all-equity sale and senior guarantee release. Ordinary dispositions require senior permission and no express junior prohibition. A cash bid buys **Collateral**, not senior debt; junior credit bidding requires cash sufficient to cause senior discharge. No standalone debt-buyout option is identified in the examined ICA; other documents remain missing (§3.1(e), §6.12).
### Recovery intake conclusion

The positive finding is contractual access asymmetry, not a quantified loss. Conditionally, declaration/demand and receipt initiate restrictions; loss of unilateral realization timing is the first legal break. If assets deteriorate during delay, senior accruals or qualifying financing could absorb more proceeds; a conditioned sale/release could replace guarantee/asset access with residual proceeds. Observable tests are notices, diligence/stay filings, claims, valuations, DIP/AP orders, sale consideration and discharge records—not assumed issuer events.

The strongest countercase combines reciprocal grants and matching-collateral intent, residual proceeds, qualified payments, conditional bidding/AP rights and anti-disproportionate-amendment safeguards (§§2.3–2.4,5.3). It wins economically if verified coextensive perfected coverage, immaterial exceptions and ample net value after actual senior claims are demonstrated. Control asymmetry alone cannot defeat that case or establish the fulcrum.
